newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland does not plan new flood tax in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Poland does not plan new flood tax in 1998.

text.p: Poland's finance ministry is not planning to introduce a new flood tax in next year's budget to help rebuild flood damaged regions, but it may change its mind, Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Wednesday.

"We are now building the (1998) budget in a way that an additional (flood) tax is not needed, but if it is needed such a possibility of course exists," Belka told a special parliamentary session on funding flood relief.
Belka said that, if a new tax was introduced, which was unlikely, it would be temporary and such inflows would be kept separate from other budgetary revenue.
Earlier on Wednesday, Belka said the government's proposed 2.5 billion zloty flood relief credit from the National Bank of Poland would not increase total budgetary spending in 1997.
Poland also plans to tap the World Bank for a $300 million credit to help relief efforts after a devastating flood covered more than one percent of the country under water.
